executionPlan.policy: Milestones are dependency gates, not feature-name checklists. A downstream milestone may start in parallel only where it does not consume an unfinished contract.

milestones.nextAction: Keep every new live row assigned at creation, then require one paired green GitHub verify/browser run on the exact pushed revision before restoring this milestone to complete; the browser repair and the narrowed stable-governance topology are implemented but not remotely discharged.

The earlier depth-one checkout checkpoint is superseded: implemented capability and semantic-authority history guards require an actual first parent, so software/governance/release verify jobs now fetch depth two and refuse missing history. Per-job scaffold tests bind that requirement; there is no verification-time fetch or new pre-push gate. Live work remains assigned and the roadmap exposes incomplete consumers. A paired green GitHub verify/browser run on the exact pushed revision still awaits authorized publication, so this milestone remains active.
